parts.note: Both give y = 0.25 at x = -1.5 and y = 7.45 at x = 2.5. Moderator recomputed every table entry: all twelve are exact at 2 d.p. (8, 5.05, 2.5, 0.25, -2, -5.75, 6.25, 4, 4.25, 5.5, 7.45, 10).

key_verdict: Key and blind examiner agree on every part; no disputes to adjudicate.
fixes: Replace 'Using a scale of 2 cm to 1 unit on the x-axis and 1 cm to 1 unit on the y-axis, draw the graph of ...' with the 4052 wording 'On the grid, draw the graph of y = x^2 + 3/x for -3 <= x <= 3.' — the grid already carries numbered axes, so the scale sentence is redundant and reads as the older 4016/4048 register.

Drop the stem sentence '(c) Use your graph to answer parts (i), (ii) and (iii). [6]' (SEAB prints marks only on leaf parts) and fold the instruction into the parts: '(c)(i) By drawing a tangent, find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 2. [2]', '(ii) Use your graph to explain why the equation ... has only one solution. [1]', '(iii) By drawing a suitable straight line on the grid, solve ... [3]'.
why: Sound question: exact table, consistent scales, an A4-sized window (12 cm by 16 cm), a derivable line, correct 2+3+2+1+3 = 11 mark split, and a different function family and equations from every exemplar (the explain-then-suitable-line pairing is the standard template, shared with 2024 but not a re-skin of it). Two wording edits — the dated scale sentence and the aggregate-marked stem — keep it off a 5.
